body.statement: Whenever \(n\le\sqrt m/(20a_m^2)\), \[\mathfrak A_{n,m}\asymp\max\{1,a_m\sqrt n\}.\] A single full-range interval pair attains the upper bound, and a mean-preserving full-corner mixture gives the matching lower bound over all measurable, optionally randomized members of \(\mathcal I_{n,m}\). At the upper boundary of this regime the factor has order \(m^{1/4}\).
body.justification: The result proves that simultaneous adaptation can be polynomially costly even though every fixed profile has an honest oracle procedure.
body.gap: CaiLow2004 organizes adaptation across linear-functional classes; it does not establish this nonlinear full-profile oracle ratio or the \(m^{1/4}\) obstruction.
body.consumer: It warns applied users that one fixed smooth-bound interval cannot be judged by pointwise approximation error alone.
